5. By the end of the period, the aquarium was the most visited attraction.

(Graph

1. Numbers belong in the body, not the overview. (2) An opinion and a reason that the graph does not show.
(3) No overall trend for each line, and the museum is missing.
Fixed
(7-style): "Overall, the aquarium grew the fastest and became the most visited attraction by 2025, while
visitor numbers at the zoo fell steadily throughout the period."
Graph
A
introduction
and
overview
·
Band
6-style
The line graph shows the number of visitors to a museum, a zoo and an aquarium from 2000 to 2025. Overall,
the aquarium had the most visitors with 205,000 in 2025, and the zoo had the least. The museum was also
popular.
Why
6-style: the introduction paraphrases, but the overview uses a number, leaves out the zoo's trend and calls
the museum "popular" without a feature.
Graph
A
introduction
and
overview
·
Band
7-style
The line graph illustrates how many people visited three attractions in a coastal city between 2000 and 2025.
Overall, the aquarium grew the fastest and became the most visited attraction by the end of the period, while
visitor numbers at the zoo fell steadily.
Why
7-style: two clear features with no numbers; the museum could be included.

Graph
A
introduction
and
overview
·
Band
8-style
The graph compares annual visitor numbers at a city's museum, zoo and aquarium over a 25-year period. The
most striking trend is the rapid rise of the aquarium, which had overtaken both older attractions by the end of
the period, less than twenty years after opening; by contrast, the zoo declined throughout, while the museum
grew overall despite one sharp temporary fall.
Why
8-style: every line's overall trend in two sentences, ranked by importance, with no ﬁgures.
Museum
body
paragraph
·
Band
7-style
The museum followed a more uneven pattern. Visitor numbers rose steadily from 120,000 in 2000 to 165,000 in
2010 and stayed at about that level until 2015. They then fell sharply to 95,000 in 2020, before recovering to a
peak of 175,000 in 2025. This ﬁnal ﬁgure was higher than the zoo's but still 30,000 below the aquarium's.

and 2025. Overall, water used for showers and baths increased, whereas the amounts used for garden watering
and laundry fell, with the sharpest drop in garden use.
